column2: 中古英语 werre ← 晚期古英语 werre ← 诺曼法语 werre（古法语 guerre）← 中世纪拉丁语 werra ← 法兰克语 *werru（混乱、争执）← 原始印欧语 *wers-（搅乱）；逐步取代了古英语 beadu、hild、wīġ 等本土词
column3: armed fighting between countries or groups
column5: The war lasted four years.|Two neighbouring states are at war.
column6: organized armed fighting between whole sides – 整方与整方之间有组织的武力相攻
column7: 战争：国家或集团间的武力冲突|交战：正在打这件事的状态

column2: 由 ware（货物）＋ house（屋）复合而成；ware 一支 ← 古英语 waru（货物）← 原始日耳曼语 *warō
column3: a large building where goods are stored
column5: The goods sit in a warehouse near the docks.|They converted the warehouse into flats.
column6: a large building kept for holding goods until needed – 专用来存货、等要用时再取的大房子
column7: 货栈：存放待售货物的那种房子|库房：泛指用于储存的屋室

column2: 由 war ＋ fare（行、往）复合而成，或截自中古英语 werre-faringe（出征）
column3: the activity of fighting a war, or the methods used
column5: Trench warfare dominated that conflict.|They turned to economic warfare instead.
column6: the carrying on of fighting, and how it is carried on – 打仗这件事的进行，以及怎么打
column7: 战事：正在进行的战斗活动|作战方式：所采用的那套打法

column2: 中古英语 warm ← 古英语 wearm ← 原始日耳曼语 *warmaz ← 原始印欧语 *gʷʰer-（热）；与希腊语 thermos 同源
column3: at a pleasant temperature between cool and hot
column5: Keep the milk warm, not hot.|She gave us a warm welcome.
column6: at the temperature that feels comfortable, short of hot – 温度舒适，还没到烫
column7: 暖的：温度适中偏高|温暖的：同义，多形容天气或环境|热情的：把这份暖用到待人的态度上

column2: 中古英语 warmth ← 古英语 *wiermþu ← 原始西日耳曼语 *warmiþu，即 warm ＋ 抽象名词后缀 -th
column3: the state of being warm, or friendly feeling
column5: The warmth of the fire filled the room.|He spoke with real warmth about her.
column6: the comfortable heat something gives off – 一件东西放出的那份舒适热度
column7: 暖意：可感到的那份温热|温情：把这份暖用到人与人之间的情意上

column2: 中古英语 warnen ← 古英语 warnian（留意、告诫）← 原始日耳曼语 *warnōną ← 原始印欧语 *wer-（察觉、留心）
column3: to tell someone about a danger in advance
column5: He warned us about the loose step.|Signs warn drivers of falling rocks.
column6: telling someone in advance so they can take care – 事先告知，让对方留心
column7: 警告：告知危险，语气重|提醒：把该留意的事点给对方

column2: 中古英语 warant（庇护、保障）← 盎格鲁诺曼语 warrant ← 古法语 garant（保证、许可）← 法兰克语 *warand，是 *warjan（挡开、阻止）的现在分词
column3: an official document giving legal authority, or good reason for something
column5: Police obtained a search warrant.|Her behaviour warrants an inquiry.
column6: an official backing that makes an action allowable – 官方给的那份靠背，使某个动作站得住
column7: 授权令：官方签发、许可行事的那份文件|正当理由：使某事说得过去的那个依据

column2: 中古英语 wasshen ← 古英语 wascan（洗）← 原始西日耳曼语 *waskan ← 原始日耳曼语 *waskaną（洗、弄湿）← 原始印欧语 *wed-（水、湿）
column3: to clean something with water
column5: Wash your hands before eating.|Waves washed the sand away.
column6: cleaning by letting water carry the dirt off – 让水把脏东西带走，从而变干净
column7: 洗：用水去污|清洗：更彻底地洗一遍|冲刷：水流不断带走表面之物

column2: 中古英语 wast ← 诺曼法语 wast ← 法兰克语 *wōstī（荒芜）← 原始印欧语 *h₁weh₂-（空、荒）
column3: to use something without good purpose, or unwanted material
column5: Do not waste water in summer.|The factory dumps its waste in the river.
column6: letting something go without being put to use – 让东西白白流失，没用到该用处
column7: 浪费：把可用的用掉却没起作用|废弃物：用剩下、不再要的那些|荒地：闲着不长东西的那片地

column2: 名词 ← 中古英语 wacche ← 古英语 wæċċe（守夜）；动词 ← 中古英语 wacchen ← 古英语 wæċċan ← 原始日耳曼语 *wakjaną（唤醒、守望）
column3: to look at something for a time, or a small clock worn on the wrist
column5: They watched the boats leave harbour.|My watch is two minutes slow.
column6: keeping the eyes on something over a stretch of time – 眼睛在一段时间里一直盯着
column7: 注视：持续看着某处|手表：戴在腕上报时的那件小钟，本义与守夜同支|看守：为防出事而盯着

column2: 中古英语 water ← 古英语 wæter ← 原始日耳曼语 *watōr ← 原始印欧语 *wódr̥（水）
column3: the clear liquid that falls as rain and fills seas
column5: Pour the water into a jug.|She waters the plants each morning.
column6: the clear liquid all living things need to drink – 一切生物都要喝的那种透明液体
column7: 水：那种液体本身|浇水：把它施到植物根上这个动作

column2: 中古英语 waterfal ← 古英语 wæterġefeall，即 water ＋ fall
column3: a place where a river drops over a steep edge
column5: The waterfall can be heard from the path.|Mist rose from the foot of the waterfall.
column6: a river dropping straight over a steep edge – 河水从陡边直落下去

column2: 由 water ＋ -proof（防…的）构成；proof 一支 ← 古法语 prueve ← 晚期拉丁语 proba（检验）
column3: not letting water pass through
column5: She wore a waterproof jacket.|The seal keeps the case waterproof.
column6: made so that water cannot get through – 做得让水过不去
column7: 防水的：能挡住水，不被浸透|不透水的：材料本身不让水通过

column2: 以苏格兰工程师 James Watt 之名命名
column3: the unit used to measure electrical power
column5: The bulb uses only nine watts.|A kettle draws about two thousand watts.
column6: the unit that measures how fast energy is used – 计量能量消耗快慢的那个单位
column7: 瓦特：这个单位的全称|瓦：日常与标注中的简称

column2: 中古英语 waven ← 古英语 wafian（摆动、挥）← 原始日耳曼语 *wabōną（摇、荡）← 原始印欧语 *webʰ-（来回动）
column3: to move the hand to and fro, or a ridge of moving water
column5: She waved from the far platform.|Waves broke over the sea wall.
column6: something moving to and fro, rising and falling as it goes – 一件东西来回摆动，边走边起落
column7: 挥手：手来回摆动作招呼|波浪：水面成排起落的那些峰|起伏：把这种一起一落用到别的事物上

column2: 中古英语 wax ← 古英语 weax ← 原始日耳曼语 *wahsą，或出自原始印欧语 *woḱ-so-
column3: a soft solid substance that melts easily, used in candles
column5: The candle is made of beeswax.|He waxed the floor until it shone.
column6: a soft solid that turns to liquid with a little heat – 稍一加热就化成液体的软固体
column7: 蜡：那种物质本身|打蜡：把它涂到表面上这个动作

column2: 中古英语 wey ← 古英语 weġ（路）← 原始日耳曼语 *wegaz ← 原始印欧语 *weǵʰ-（走、运）
column3: a route from one place to another, or a manner of doing something
column5: Ask someone the way to the station.|There must be a better way to do this.
column6: the line one follows to get somewhere or get something done – 到某处或办成某事所循的那条线
column7: 路：从此处通往彼处的路线|方法：办成一件事所循的路子|做法：具体怎么办的那一套

column2: 中古英语 waik，借自古诺尔斯语 veikr（弱的）← 原始日耳曼语 *waikwaz（易弯的、屈从的）← 原始印欧语 *weyg-（弯、转）
column3: lacking strength, or easily broken
column5: He felt weak after the illness.|This tea is far too weak.
column6: giving way instead of holding – 一受力就让开，而不是撑住
column7: 弱的：力气或程度不足|不结实的：受力就坏|淡的：所含成分少，作用不强

column2: 中古英语 welth ← 古英语 *welþu ← 原始西日耳曼语 *waliþu；或为 wele（安康、富足）受 helth、derth 一类 -th 词影响而成 ← 原始印欧语 *wel-（好）
column3: a large amount of money and possessions
column5: The family's wealth came from shipping.|A wealth of detail fills the report.
column6: holdings large enough that one need not want – 家底厚到不必缺什么
column7: 财富：所拥有的钱与财产|丰厚：把这份多用到别的事物上，指数量可观

column2: 中古英语 welthy，即 wealth ＋ 形容词后缀 -y
column3: having a great deal of money
column5: A wealthy buyer took the whole lot.|The district is noticeably wealthy.
column6: holding far more than is needed to live – 手里的远超过生活所需
column7: 富有的：钱财多|富裕的：生活宽裕，多形容地区或家庭

column2: 中古英语 wepen ← 古英语 wǣpn ← 原始日耳曼语 *wēpną（兵器），更早词源不明
column3: a thing made or used for fighting
column5: Police found no weapon at the scene.|Words became her only weapon.
column6: a thing taken up in order to strike or defend – 拿起来用于攻或守的那件东西
column7: 武器：用于攻防的器械|兵器：偏指冷兵器那一类

column2: 中古英语 weren ← 古英语 werian（穿、覆）← 原始日耳曼语 *wazjaną（穿衣）← 原始印欧语 *wes-（着装）；与拉丁语 vestis 同源
column3: to have clothes on the body, or to become thinner from use
column5: She wore a grey coat.|The steps have worn smooth over the years.
column6: having something on the body, or being rubbed thin by use – 把东西着在身上，或因反复使用而变薄
column7: 穿着：衣服着在身上|戴：帽子首饰之类着在身上|耗损：长期摩擦使表面变薄

column2: 中古英语 wery ← 古英语 wēriġ（疲乏的）← 原始西日耳曼语 *wōrīg
column3: very tired, or tired of something
column5: They arrived weary and hungry.|She grew weary of his excuses.
column6: worn down until neither body nor patience is left – 耗到体力与耐性都不剩
column7: 疲惫的：体力耗尽|厌倦的：耐性耗尽，不想再听再做

column2: 中古英语 weder ← 古英语 weder ← 原始日耳曼语 *wedrą ← 原始印欧语 *h₂weh₁-（吹）
column3: the state of the air at a place and time
column5: The weather turned cold overnight.|Bad weather delayed the flight.
column6: how the air is behaving at a place just now – 某地此刻空气的状况
column7: 天气：眼下的冷暖晴雨|天候：一段时期内的气候状况

column2: 中古英语 weven ← 古英语 wefan（织）← 原始西日耳曼语 *weban ← 原始日耳曼语 *webaną ← 原始印欧语 *webʰ-（编、织）
column3: to make cloth by crossing threads over and under
column5: She weaves cloth on a hand loom.|He wove between the parked cars.
column6: crossing strands over and under until they hold together – 让线一上一下交叉，直到彼此扣住
column7: 织：用织机把线交织成布|编：用条状物交叉成器|穿行：在障碍间左右绕过，路线像织线一样交错

column2: 中古英语 web ← 古英语 webb ← 原始日耳曼语 *wabją（织物、网）← *webaną（织）← 原始印欧语 *webʰ-（编、织）
column3: a net of fine threads made by a spider, or a system of connected things
column5: A spider's web hung across the gate.|The city has a web of narrow lanes.
column6: fine strands crossing to form a connected net – 细丝交叉成一张彼此相连的网
column7: 蛛网：蜘蛛吐丝结成的那张网|网状物：形状类似的那种交错结构|网络：互相连通的整套系统

column2: 中古英语 wedding ← 古英语 weddung（订婚、成婚），即 wed ＋ -ing；wed 一支 ← 古英语 weddian（立誓、许配）
column3: the ceremony at which two people marry
column5: Their wedding took place in June.|She wore her mother's wedding dress.
column6: the ceremony in which two people pledge to each other – 两人彼此立誓的那场仪式
column7: 婚礼：举行的那场仪式|结婚典礼：同一场仪式，说得更正式

column2: 中古英语 wegge ← 古英语 weċġ（楔）← 原始西日耳曼语 *wagi ← 原始日耳曼语 *wagjaz
column3: a piece of wood or metal thick at one end and thin at the other
column5: He drove a wedge into the crack.|A car was wedged between two vans.
column6: a shape thick at one end that forces things apart as it goes in – 一头厚一头薄，插进去就把东西撑开
column7: 楔子：那件一头厚一头薄的物件|楔入：把它插进去挤紧这个动作

column2: 中古英语 weed ← 古英语 wēod（野草）← 原始西日耳曼语 *weud
column3: a wild plant growing where it is not wanted
column5: Weeds had taken over the beds.|He spent the morning weeding.
column6: a plant growing where nobody planted it – 没人种它，它却长在那里
column7: 野草：不请自来的那些草|除草：把它们拔掉这个动作

column2: 中古英语 wyke ← 古英语 wice ← 原始日耳曼语 *wikǭ（序列、周）← 原始印欧语 *weyk-（弯、转）；与 weak 同支，本义指循环往复
column3: a period of seven days
column5: He will be away for a week.|We meet twice a week.
column6: a run of seven days that repeats – 七天一轮、循环往复的那一段
column7: 周：七天为一轮的那个单位|星期：同义，日常口语多用
